assertion_analysis.failure_condition: test_a_discarded_request_is_reported_nowhere (tests/test_a_discarded_request_stays_discarded.py:148) asserts _stream_rows(run_id) == []; it reddens exactly when _report_queued_failure appends a stream row for a run whose discard is recorded, which is the regression the node guards. It is independently sourced (rows written by production code on one side, the empty expectation on the other) and the node's own negative-control.log shows it failing with the discard check removed from _report_queued_failure (FAILED ...::test_a_discarded_request_is_reported_nowhere, EXIT=1, against 4 passed), so the assertion is falsifiable and not a self-comparison.

test_a_kept_request_is_reported_once_as_queued (tests/test_a_discarded_request_stays_discarded.py:168-171) asserts len(rows) == 1, rows[0]['to_state'] == 'queued' and pointer.get('failure_reported_at'); it reddens if the report stops appending (len 0), appends twice (len 2) or the marker is not stamped. It also serves as the positive control for the sibling empty assertion: the same _stream_rows helper sees the one row that is known to be present, so the helper's filter is shown to work before the empty result is reported.

call_sites: reckon/crew_run_commands.py:3383 queue_admission.admit_until_stopped is the production admit entry

findings.text: follow-on: the added _stream_rows(run_id) duplicates a capability the suite already owns. tests/test_a_held_request_stays_queued.py:74 defines _stream_file_rows(project, run_id) — "The rows the project's watch stream carries for one run id" — reading runs.watch_stream_path(project), returning [] when the file is absent, and filtering rows by run_id; the new helper does the same over PROJECT. The owning file is in the same gate command and the node's test file already imports from a sibling test module (tests/test_a_queued_run_is_admitted), so _stream_file_rows could have been imported rather than forked. It duplicates rather than extends the owner. The name _stream_rows also collides with the differently-shaped _stream_rows(before, after) in tests/test_a_held_request_stays_queued.py:58. Does not hold the node: the guard it supports is real and green.
